text: Plan around the retirement date of Plover-9: July 4, 2028 is when it goes dark.
Unlike Godwit-3, whose language is handled elsewhere, the language of Swift-4 is Swift. Nobody should assume the language of Swift-4 applies to Godwit-3, the language differs.
Unlike Plover-9, whose port is handled elsewhere, the port of Siskin-9 is 9195. Nobody should assume the port of Siskin-9 applies to Plover-9, the port differs.
Questions about Godwit-3 start with its owner, the Trellis team; they triage anything filed against it. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
The rate limit of Siskin-9 is 900 requests per minute; callers over it get a 429.
Bittern-5 was granted a budget of $2640k this year; an unspent budget does not roll over.
Swift-4 has one owner, the Harbor team, which approves each release and keeps the runbook current. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
The retirement date for Osprey-7 is May 19, 2029; after that day it stops serving. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
The service Swift-4 takes traffic on port 7808, and the port is fixed across every environment.

Unlike Godwit-3, whose pager rotation is handled elsewhere, the pager rotation of Plover-9 is Jolene Abernathy. Nobody should assume the pager rotation of Plover-9 applies to Godwit-3, the pager rotation differs.
Unlike Swift-4, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Bittern-5 is the Quill team. Nobody should assume the owner of Bittern-5 applies to Swift-4, the owner differs.
For Bittern-5 the port is 6376. Changing the port needs a change ticket. The page was last reviewed in the spring.
The yearly budget for Osprey-7 is $835k, covering licences and hosting.
The language of Godwit-3 is Elixir, which new contributors must know.
Plover-9 listens on port 5169; anyone who cannot reach that port should check the firewall rules.
The service Osprey-7 takes traffic on port 3928, and the port is fixed across every environment. Details change slowly, so check the history first.
Unlike Swift-4, whose language is handled elsewhere, the language of Plover-9 is Rust. Nobody should assume the language of Plover-9 applies to Swift-4, the language differs.
The yearly budget for Swift-4 is $1545k, covering licences and hosting. An older draft of this note was archived.
Plan around the retirement date of Godwit-3: March 6, 2027 is when it goes dark.
Godwit-3 runs in the Cairo datacenter, next to its database. The page was last reviewed in the spring.
Questions about Osprey-7 start with its owner, the Ember team; they triage anything filed against it.
Talia Nakamura is on the pager rotation of Swift-4 this month, with a deputy as backup. The entry was reformatted last quarter.

Unlike Siskin-9, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Bittern-5 is the Oslo datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Bittern-5 applies to Siskin-9, the datacenter differs.

Unlike Osprey-7, whose budget is handled elsewhere, the budget of Siskin-9 is $3420k. Nobody should assume the budget of Siskin-9 applies to Osprey-7, the budget differs. Details change slowly, so check the history first.

Unlike Plover-9, whose pager rotation is handled elsewhere, the pager rotation of Godwit-3 is Mateo Underhill. Nobody should assume the pager rotation of Godwit-3 applies to Plover-9, the pager rotation differs.

Unlike Bittern-5, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Siskin-9 is the Lima datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Siskin-9 applies to Bittern-5, the datacenter differs.

Unlike Plover-9, whose retirement date is handled elsewhere, the retirement date of Siskin-9 is September 7, 2028. Nobody should assume the retirement date of Siskin-9 applies to Plover-9, the retirement date differs.
Unlike Swift-4, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Plover-9 is the Ledger team. Nobody should assume the owner of Plover-9 applies to Swift-4, the owner differs.
Jolene Fairbanks is on the pager rotation of Osprey-7 this month, with a deputy as backup.
